HOST portrait: Strice Foods Host — a corporate Matrix system rendered as cyberspace architecture, NOT a person and NOT a creature. Strice Foods is a mid-tier Seattle food corporation running a deliberately low-cost system (Orange-4). Sculpt it as a cold industrial food-processing plant reimagined in the Matrix: monolithic vats, conveyor lines and silo forms built from luminous wireframe and grid-mapped planes, receding into black void. A corporate logo motif glows at the centre like a system core. Sterile, cheap, functional — the digital equivalent of a cannery, not a glamorous megacorp cathedral. Palette: cold steel and grey-green with amber warning glow; avoid purple.

PERSON portrait: Pride (Shaka Jubowel). An African shaman turned globally active shadowrunner specialising in bounty-hunting, named for the conqueror Shaka Zulu. Almost two metres tall with a heavily muscular frame, very black skin, long stringy hair growing down the back of his neck. CRUCIAL DETAIL: his eyes have VERTICAL SLIT PUPILS like a cat's — his Lion totem showing through. He wears real leather clothing of African design, worn and practical. Bearing of an aristocrat: proud, composed, watchful, cunning — but with something savage held just beneath it. Warm earth palette, ochre and deep bronze and firelight; avoid purple.

PERSON portrait: Vincent Burroughs. A mid-level corporate man at Strice Foods — the Security Director's contact, and a man being quietly blackmailed. Soft, unathletic, office-pale, early forties, thinning hair, a cheap but carefully-kept corporate suit. A datajack at his temple. He is NOT a fighter and should not look like one: the expression is anxious and evasive, a man who checks who is behind him. Cold fluorescent office lighting, drab grey-green corporate palette.

PERSON portrait: The Strice Boys. A Strice Foods facility guard — better equipped and harder than a lobby rent-a-cop. Armored vest with visible ceramic trauma plates over a company uniform, an Uzi submachine gun held ready, a stun baton on the belt. Broad, physical, unimpressed, working-class muscle who has done this a while. Industrial warehouse lighting, sodium-amber and cold steel.
